faqs.question: I am unable to connect my product to a wireless network. What should I do?
faqs.answer: The printer does not come with built-in wireless features and does not support a wireless (or Ethernet) connection to a network router. Only a direct wired connection to the computer is supported.

faqs.question: How do I obtain the latest product software for Windows or my Mac?
faqs.answer: You can download the latest product driver from the Downloads section of this website.

faqs.question: Can the Epson ink cartridges be refilled or can I use third-party ink cartridges without voiding the warranty?
faqs.answer:
Epson does not recommend refilling or using other brands of ink cartridges.  Epson uses a permanent Micro Piezo print head that has allowed Epson to lead the industry in delivering consistent photo image quality by using variable-sized droplets.  Micro Piezo print head can also use a wider variety of inks, which has allowed Epson to introduce such ink breakthroughs as DURABrite® and Epson UltraChrome® inks that offer greatly improved humidity resistance, smudge resistance, and fade resistance.
Using refilled ink cartridges will not void the product's original warranty; however, if these products cause a failure, the repair of that failure will not be covered under warranty.

faqs.question: I brought my product with me to a different country and can't find ink for it. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Some Epson printers and ink cartridges are specific to a regional market and not sold worldwide, although the same printers are sold in the U.S. and Canada. If you have a printer sold in the U.S. or Canada, you may not be able to easily get ink cartridges for it in foreign markets.
Unfortunately, because of customs and tax regulations, the Epson E-Stores in the U.S. and Canada are unable to ship to addresses outside the U.S. and Canada.

faqs.question: Can the printer still print if an ink cartridge is expended or not installed?
faqs.answer: No. The printer will not operate if any cartridge is expended or removed. It's best to always have extra cartridges on hand.

faqs.question: Does Epson have a program where I can donate my working electronic equipment?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Epson America, Inc. and
Digitunity
have joined together with the goal of helping those who are facing economic challenges or have a disability to gain access to today's technology. With your donation, you not only help the environment, but you also help change the lives of those who need these products the most.

faqs.question: Heavy coated or thick paper does not load correctly or loads skewed. What should I do?
faqs.answer: The paper you are using may be too heavy or glossy for the paper roller to pick up. Be sure the paper is within printer specifications.

faqs.question: Does my product support Epson Connect?
faqs.answer: No, your product is not compatible.

faqs.question: Does OS X support manual duplex printing with my product?
faqs.answer: This feature is not supported in Mac OS X. However, if your printer has a built-in automatic duplexer, auto-duplexing is supported in Mac OS X 10.6 (Snow Leopard).

faqs.question: My product makes noise after I turn it on or after it has been sitting for a while. What should I do?
faqs.answer: This is normal. It is performing routine maintenance.

faqs.question: How do I set up my product for the fastest printing?
faqs.answer:
If you're printing from your computer, make sure your system meets the
requirements
. If you're printing a high-resolution image, you need more than the minimum requirements listed. You may also need to:
Clear space on your hard drive or run a defragmentation utility.
Close programs that you're not using.
Increase your system's memory.
For the fastest printing, try these tips:
Choose black ink only in your printer settings if your document doesn't include color.
For Windows, choose
Draft
for the Quality Option.
For Macintosh, set the Quality/Speed slider to
Speed
.
If the printer is connected to a USB hub, disconnect unused USB devices.
Make sure
Quite Mode
is not selected.

faqs.question: How do I print a borderless photo from Windows or my Mac?
faqs.answer:
Do the following:
For Windows, click the Borderless checkbox on the
Main
tab of the printer driver. To use the borderless option, you'll need to select a compatible borderless paper size and type. See
Select Basic Options
for more details.
For a Macintosh, select a paper size with the
Sheet Feeder - Borderless
option on the Page Setup window. See
Select Page Options
for more details.

faqs.question: When I try to print to my product in Windows 7, printing is slow or my product stops printing. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following:
Select a lower quality setting in the printer software.
Make sure your system meets the minimum system requirements for your printer.
Close the
Devices and Printers
window before you print.
Clear space on your hard drive or run a defragmentation utility.
Close programs that you're not using.
Increase your system's memory.

faqs.question: Does OS X support manual duplex printing with my product?
faqs.answer: This feature is not supported in Mac OS X. However, if your printer has a built-in automatic duplexer, auto-duplexing is supported in Mac OS X 10.6 (Snow Leopard).

faqs.question: I replaced an ink cartridge and my product shows that the same ink cartridge is expended. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Follow these steps to make sure the cartridges are correctly installed:
Make sure the printer is turned on. (The green power light should be on, but not flashing.) Then open the printer cover.
Press and release the ink button. The print head moves to the
position to indicate which cartridge should be reinstalled.
Note
: Don't hold down the ink button for more than 2 seconds, or the printer will start to clean the print head.
Caution
: To avoid damaging the printer, never move the print head by hand.
Press the ink button again.
If another cartridge needs to be reinstalled, it moves to the
position. Press the ink button again to see if other cartridges need to be reinstalled.
If no other cartridges need to be reinstalled, the print head moves to the replacement position on the right.
Press down all the ink cartridges until they click into place to make sure they are properly seated.
Note
: If a cartridge is properly seated already, you may not hear a click.
Close the cartridge cover.
Close the printer cover and press the ink button. The printer begins charging the ink. This takes about 1 1/2 minutes.
When the power light stops flashing and remains on, ink charging is finished.
Caution
: Never turn off the printer while the power light is flashing, or you'll waste ink.

faqs.answer:
See
Replace Ink Cartridges
.

faqs.question: How do I know when an ink cartridge needs to be replaced?
faqs.answer:
When the ink replace light is on, the printer will require you to change the cartridge. You need to replace a cartridge when it's expended or it gets too old. See
Replace Ink Cartridges

Caution:

Do not open ink cartridge packages until you are ready to install the ink. Cartridges are vacuum packed to maintain reliability.

faqs.question: How long should an ink cartridge remain in my product if it's not used often?
faqs.answer: When an installed ink cartridge is more than six months old, you may need to replace it if you notice that your printouts don't look as good as they used to and quality doesn't improve after cleaning and aligning the print head.

faqs.question: I installed new ink cartridges and my product seems to be doing a long cleaning cycle. Is this normal?
faqs.answer:
Yes. It takes about 1½ minutes for the printer to charge the ink delivery system when you install or replace the ink cartridges.
Note:
Never turn off the printer while it is charging the ink delivery system (unless the printer hasn't moved or made noise for more than 5 minutes). This initialization is a normal and necessary process. If the printer initialization does not stop after 5 minutes, turn the printer off and contact Epson technical support for assistance.

faqs.answer:
Epson does not recommend refilling or using other brands of ink cartridges.  Epson uses a permanent Micro Piezo print head that has allowed Epson to lead the industry in delivering consistent photo image quality by using variable-sized droplets.  Micro Piezo print head can also use a wider variety of inks, which has allowed Epson to introduce such ink breakthroughs as DURABrite® and Epson UltraChrome® inks that offer greatly improved humidity resistance, smudge resistance, and fade resistance.
Using refilled ink cartridges will not void the product's original warranty; however, if these products cause a failure, the repair of that failure will not be covered under warranty.

faqs.question: Can the printer still print if an ink cartridge is expended or not installed?
faqs.answer: No. The printer will not operate if any cartridge is expended or removed. It's best to always have extra cartridges on hand.

faqs.question: I brought my product with me to a different country and can't find ink for it. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Some Epson printers and ink cartridges are specific to a regional market and not sold worldwide, although the same printers are sold in the U.S. and Canada. If you have a printer sold in the U.S. or Canada, you may not be able to easily get ink cartridges for it in foreign markets.
Unfortunately, because of customs and tax regulations, the Epson E-Stores in the U.S. and Canada are unable to ship to addresses outside the U.S. and Canada.

faqs.question: I'm having paper feed problems. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
If paper doesn't feed, remove it from the sheet feeder. Reload it against the right side, behind the tab. Then press in the tab on the edge guide and slide it against the paper, and make sure it's not too tight. Make sure the paper is not above the arrow mark inside the edge guide.
If multiple pages feed at once, remove the paper from the sheet feeder, fan the edges to separate the sheets, then reload it.
Make sure you don't load more than the recommended number of sheets. If you're printing on both sides of the paper, try loading fewer sheets.
Paper type

Epson Bright White Paper

and 8 × 10”)
or
10 sheets
(for 4 × 6”
and 5 × 7”)
Epson Premium Photo Paper Semi-gloss
Epson Premium Presentation Paper Matte

Epson Photo Quality Self-Adhesive Sheets

Make sure you use new, smooth, high-quality paper, that is not curled, creased, old, or too thin. Load it printable side up.
If the paper doesn't eject fully, you may have selected the wrong paper size in the printer software. Press the
paper button to eject the paper. Select the correct paper size when you reprint.
If it's wrinkled when it is ejected, the paper may be damp or too thin. Load new paper.
If the paper jams, do the following:
Gently pull any jammed paper out from the output tray or sheet feeder.
Try turning the printer off and then back on, to eject the jammed paper.
If that doesn't work and paper is stuck inside, turn off the printer. Open the printer cover, remove the jammed paper and torn pieces, close the cover, and turn the printer back on.

faqs.question: What is the best media to use for everyday printing?
faqs.answer:
Epson recommends using plain photocopy or bond papers for your everyday printing. If you would like to use higher quality paper, we recommend using
Epson Bright White Paper
or
Epson Presentation Paper Matte
.
Epson Bright White Paper
is a 24lb paper with a sleek, ultra-smooth surface, and 108+ brightness. This paper delivers crisp black text and vivid, colorful images. It can also be used for two-sided printing.
Epson Presentation Paper Matte
is a 45lb ultra-smooth, bright white heavyweight paper, with a matte finish and 97 brightness. This paper is perfect for B&W photos, enlargements and cherished photos.

faqs.question: Does the type of paper I use really make a difference?
faqs.answer:
The type of paper you choose affects the way your printout looks, so be sure to select the correct paper for your print job. If you are just making a copy or printing a rough draft of an image, plain paper is fine. However, for the best results, you'll want to use one of Epson's special ink jet papers designed for your printer. See
Available Epson Papers for the Epson Stylus C120
.

faqs.question: Can I use sheet labels with my product?
faqs.answer:
You can use Epson's
Photo Quality Self Adhesive Sheets
. A cutting grid is printed on the reverse side of each sheet for easy custom trimming (such as labels). To avoid paper jams, load only one sheet at a time. Also, set the
Type
or
Media Type
setting in the driver to
Premium Presentation Paper Matte
.

faqs.question: How do I know which paper or media type to select in my product's driver?
faqs.answer:
See
Paper or Media Type Settings for Loaded Paper
.

faqs.question: What kind of paper gives the best results for high quality printing?
faqs.answer: For the best results, you'll want to use one of Epson's special ink jet papers designed for your printer.

faqs.question: How should I load envelopes?
faqs.answer:
See
Load Envelopes
.

faqs.question: How can I stop my product from feeding multiple pages at the same time?
faqs.answer: If multiple pages feed at once, remove the paper from the sheet feeder, fan the edges to separate the sheets, then reload it.

faqs.question: Heavy coated or thick paper does not load correctly or loads skewed. What should I do?
faqs.answer: The paper you are using may be too heavy or glossy for the paper roller to pick up. Be sure the paper is within printer specifications.

faqs.question: The quality of my printed output is unacceptable. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
If your output does not look good but the image looks fine on your computer screen, make sure you select the correct quality option, paper type, paper size and orientation setting in the printer driver for your print job. See
Select Basic Options
for Windows or
Select Basic Print Options
for Macintosh.
If that doesn't help, see
Print Quality Problems
.

faqs.question: My printout has incorrect margins. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
Make sure the paper settings are correct for your paper size in the printer software.
Choose the correct margins for your paper size in your printing program.
Use the
Print Preview
option in your  printer software to check your margins before you print.
Make sure your paper is positioned next to the right side of the feeder. See
Loading paper
.
If you're using a Macintosh, make sure you choose the correct printer in the Page Setup window and the Print window.
If you're printing from a web browser, the pages may not print correctly due to the web page design. Try one of the following:
Check to see if there is a
Printer Friendly Version
(or similarly named) icon or link on the web page that you can click on.
Experiment with page setup and paper size, then select
Print Preview
from the File menu in your application to view the changes.

faqs.question: My product is printing blank pages. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
Make sure the
print head nozzles
are not clogged.
The ink cartridges may be old or low on ink, and you may need to
replace them
.
Try printing a different document to determine if the problem is limited to one document. If it is, you may need to recreate your original document (by copying and pasting the text into a new file for example).

faqs.question: My printout has lines running through it. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following:
Clean
the print head nozzles.
Select a higher
Quality Option
or
Print Quality
and turn off
High Speed
mode in the printer software.
Make sure the paper Type or Media Type setting matches the paper you loaded.
Make sure the printable side of the paper is face up. It's usually brighter or whiter.
Replace
the ink cartridges.
On a Macintosh, try using
Automatic
mode.
Align
the print head.

faqs.question: My printout has incorrect or missing colors. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
The problem could be due to a software setting, the condition of the printer, or the paper you're using. Check the following:
Make sure the ink setting in your printer software is not set to black ink only.
The print head nozzles may need
cleaning
.
The ink cartridges may be old or low on ink, and you may need to
replace them
.
Try turning off
PhotoEnhance
in the Windows printer software.
On a Macintosh, try using
Automatic
mode.
Try changing the
Gamma
setting in your printer software.
Your printed colors can never exactly match your on-screen colors. However, you can use a color management system to get as close as possible. Try using the ICM (Windows) or ColorSync (Macintosh) setting.
For best results, use genuine Epson ink and paper.

faqs.question: My printout is blurry or smeared. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
Make sure your paper isn't damp or curled, or loaded face down (the printable side should be face up). It's usually brighter or whiter.
Use a support sheet with special paper, or try loading your paper one sheet at a time.
Make sure your paper meets the
specifications
.
Use Epson papers to ensure proper saturation and absorption of genuine Epson inks.
Align
the print head.
Remove each sheet from the output tray as it is printed.
Avoid handling printouts on glossy paper for a few hours to allow the ink to set.
If ink smears on the back of a printout,
clean the paper path
.
Turn off
High Speed
mode in the printer software.
If you are using double-sided paper and printing heavily saturated or dark images on the front side of the paper, you may notice that smudges or marks appear on the front when you print the second side. If one side of the paper will contain a lighter image or text, print that side first to eliminate marks or smudging.

faqs.question: My printout contains garbled characters when I print from Windows or my Mac. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following:
Make sure the USB cable is securely connected and is a shielded “AB” cable not more then 6.5 feet (2 meters) long. Then try printing again.
If you're using a switch box or USB hub with your printer, connect the printer directly to your computer.
Cancel a print job if communication to the printer was interrupted in the middle of printing. (The interruption could be caused by turning the printer off and on or disconnecting and reconnecting the cable in the middle of a print job).

faqs.question: My printout is grainy when I print from any application. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Check the following:
Make sure the printable side of the paper is face up. It's usually brighter or whiter.
Select a higher
Quality Option
or
Print Quality
, and turn off
High Speed
and
Fast Economy
or
Economy
mode in the printer software.
Select
Photo RPM
for Quality Type (Windows) or Print Quality (Macintosh). Remember that this setting increases print time.
Align
the print head.
You may need to increase the image resolution or print in a smaller size; see your software documentation.
Try printing a different image to determine if the problem is limited to one image. If it is, you may need to recreate your original image.

faqs.question: The image look inverted, as if viewed in a mirror. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
You may have accidentally selected the
Mirror Image
or
Rotate 180°
option in the printer driver or a similar feature in your software application. Make sure the settings are not turned on in the printer driver or in your application program. (If you're printing on Epson Iron-On Cool Peel Transfer Paper, the image should be inverted.)
Windows
Macintosh

Check for a

Windows 2000, XP, Vista

Click
OK

Macintosh 10.5.x

Print

Save As
, enter a name for your preset, and click

Click
Print

faqs.question: My product makes noise after I turn it on or after it has been sitting for a while. What should I do?
faqs.answer: This is normal. It is performing routine maintenance.

faqs.question: Does Epson have a program where I can donate my working electronic equipment?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Epson America, Inc. and
Digitunity
have joined together with the goal of helping those who are facing economic challenges or have a disability to gain access to today's technology. With your donation, you not only help the environment, but you also help change the lives of those who need these products the most.
